main_body: A wooden-framed fish tank: brown rim, glass front filled with water, a fish, plants and a sand bed.
top_band: Rows 9-12 (4 rows): brown rim on row 9, a 2-row strip of blue water (rows 10-11, L≈139, the same family as the glass below), brown rim on row 12. No distinct lighter top surface.
evidence: Below the thin top, the glass front (rows 13-30) is a flat face-on panel: water, fish, plants and sand are painted on one plane. The only 'top' is a rim around a 2-row water strip whose tone matches the front water (L 139 vs 139), so it reads as a rim, not a surface. Row 13 has a light highlight, but there is no eave shadow and no inset on the glass. Of the 4 top rows, 2 are rim, which leaves too thin a surface. This is the rim-only fish-tank failure, a front elevation with a hat.

style.evidence: The candidate has 23 colours and 10 per tile, against 40 and 17-20 for the references. Its flat-fill coverage is 27%, against 13% and 0%. The water is two big flat blue blocks with a few single-pixel sparkles, and the sand and frame are only lightly textured. Dark edge pixels are 54% neutral, so the outline is partly near-black rather than a consistent dark material tone. It looks thinner and flatter than the stall and well.
